name: Garage door technician

pf.license.need: Garage door work needs a license where the state, county or city licenses door or home repair contractors. Some places license it only above a job amount.
pf.license.who holds it: The company, where a license is required. Each door tech only where the state's form licenses door techs.
what to ask: The company's license number and class, where the state's form asks
Each door tech's own number, in their invite reply, only where the state asks
Insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks. A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks: from the state form.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.electrical work: A new outlet or a hardwired opener circuit is electrical work. It's booked only where the company holds the electrical license the place requires; otherwise an electrician comes first.
pf.license.at the counter: Setting up remotes and keypads and repairing opener parts at the counter: the state's form says if it needs a license. Safe default: the business registration on file.
pf.license.local rules: Some cities and counties license door work or need a permit of their own, like for a new door: the form for that place applies, by the customer's address.

pf.services.capacity: One tech per booking. A new door or a heavy double door can need a crew of two. The counter's board repairs need its one test bench.
pf.services.skills each needs: Springs and cables, openers, new doors and gates are separate skills. Board repairs at the counter need the board skill.
pf.services.nobody home: Never: an adult (18 or older) must be home for the whole visit, ticked on the booking page.
pf.services.online: A video check of an opener or a remote only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Every part is listed on the quote. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

stops the booking.says: Call 911 now. Don't try to lift the door yourself.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A loud bang, a broken spring, a snapped cable, or a door hanging crooked
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Don't lift the door, pull the red release cord, or touch the springs. The door is very heavy now and can drop. Keep people, pets and the car clear.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: An opener that won't stop, or won't go back up
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Unplug the opener, and keep everyone clear of the door.
Don't force the door. A tech comes first; a ride is safer if you must leave sooner.

pf.safety.Rosie's rule: Rosie never explains how to release, adjust or wind a spring. Safety answers come word for word from the business's own safety notes.
pf.safety.at the counter: Springs and lift cables are never sold at the counter for a customer to put on. A spring job is a home visit by a tech.
pf.safety.a repair declined: A part the tech marks as a danger (frayed cables, a door that can drop, an opener that fails its test) is left safe: the door shut, or the opener unplugged. The customer gets the written safety note.
pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the tech, with a photo. An adult stays home for the whole visit.
pf.visit.check-in at the counter: The code at the counter (the tech or the desk types it). A drop-off gets its code when the opener is left, and READY when it's tested.
pf.visit.quotes at the visit: The tech texts the quote with every part listed, before any work. It can be lines to say yes to one by one: springs, cables, rollers. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.springs: Springs are replaced as a pair, sized to the door's weight.
pf.visit.extra work: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A new opener or a new door gets its own quote.
pf.visit.work sold at the home: A written right to cancel for extras and new jobs sold at the home, where the rules require it. The repair the customer asked for isn't an extra.
pf.visit.safety test: After every repair, before DONE: the auto-reverse test. The door must go back up when it touches a board laid flat under it, and when the light beam is blocked. A fail: the tech resets the opener's force and travel limits and tests again. Still a fail: the opener is unplugged, the door is left working by hand, and a new opener gets its own quote.
pf.visit.before work: Photos of the door, springs and opener before work.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The tech texts DONE with the bill's lines once the test passes, and photos after.
pf.visit.permits: Where a permit was pulled for a new door, the inspector's visit is set up after the work, and the result is kept with the job.

pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the work.

pf.messages.danger words: Someone hurt or pinned under the door always gets 'call 911' first, before anything else.

pf.staff.levels: Door techs and a lead tech. A person's license only where the state licenses door techs.
skills: Doors off track, rollers and hinges
pf.staff.supervision: A helper works only with a tech on the job, and never on springs alone.
pf.staff.special work: Electrical work for a new opener only by people with that license, where the place requires one.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit and same-day urgent jobs. A job sent now goes to the tech on call, then the backup set at sign-up. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another tech with the same skill, at the same window and price.

pf.rules.written estimate: A written estimate or contract before work above an amount: from the state form.
pf.rules.right to cancel: A written right to cancel for extras and new jobs sold at the home: where the rules require it. A new job sold at the home (a new opener or door) is put in after the cancel days end, where the rules require it.
pf.rules.license on papers: The license number on the listing, quotes and bills: from the state form.
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the business for a new door where the local rules require one; the inspection follows.
pf.rules.declared emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own (the example: springs 3 years on parts, labor 1 year), shown on the receipt.
pf.rules.opener safety: Every repair ends with the auto-reverse test. A new opener has its own reversing sensors.
pf.rules.state notices: A state's own notices for home repairs: from the state form, sent before the work or with the quote.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work, with each safety test result.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for garage doors:
garage doors: A car stuck inside: marked urgent, and sent now where someone is on call
Someone hurt or pinned under the door: call 911 first, no booking
The door gets worse before the visit: the safety steps again, then urgent
Asked how to fix a spring: never explained; the safety words, word for word
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A part found worn at the visit (frayed cables): its own line on the quote; declined, it's noted with a safety note
The auto-reverse test fails: the force reset and tested again, or the opener unplugged and quoted on its own
A new opener needs a new outlet: an electrician first, unless the company holds that license
A renter whose landlord pays: the landlord's OK first, or the renter pays instead
A storm brings many calls: PAUSE, and a declared emergency's price limits
At the counter: a board that can't be repaired, a customer asking for springs, or a drop-off nobody picks up

steps.title: Andre runs the auto-reverse test
steps.q: Does the door go back up?
steps.does: After every repair or new opener, before DONE, Andre tests the safety reverse. The door must go back up when it touches a board laid flat under it, and when the light beam is blocked.
more: The plug-in names this test. DONE waits for a pass, and the result goes on the job record.
New springs change the door's balance, so the test runs after every spring job too.

notes:
Pilot: contractor-style project work at the home, with a shop counter (the example: Bayside Garage Doors and its Bayside Door Parts counter). Flow A: the customer comes to the counter (remote set-up, opener parts, the bench check); flow B: a door tech goes to the home (spring replacement, opener, door repair, visit fee, quotes).
Plug-in facts: photos, documents, extrawork, firststeps. Switches: cancelright on in flow B only (the master's B8-78 cancel window for a new job sold at the home); sensitive, welfare and no2 off (the $2 is paid, D97). Settings: arrive setstart in flow A (a counter time), window in flow B; cutoff 24 hours before.
Flow A money: list|card|counter (main; $35 remote set-up, a card saved for the shop's $20 fee, paid at the counter), list|none|counter (nothing taken), list|full|none ($55 opener gear kit, paid in full), photos|card|counter ($90 board repair from photos; Sam OKs; $20 fee), visit|card|counter (opener part repair, priced at the counter; $20 fee). The old $140 rebuild with its $40 fee is gone; a card is saved instead of any hold.
Flow B money: list|card|bill (main; $179 spring replacement; a card saved for the $89 visit fee; the bill after the job), list|none|bill ($179, nothing taken), list|card|card ($179, the card charged when DONE), visit|card|bill and visit|card|card (door off its track, priced at the visit; card saved; charged at DONE only the price OK'd), photos|deposit|bill ($640 new opener from photos; $160 deposit; $480 rest on the bill), list|full|none ($150 tune-up and safety check, paid in full). The $89 is the trip fee (the late-cancel and no-show fee), kept only up to what was paid now where money was paid.
Removed in this refit: every legacy money words op (vary keys by price, before, after), all dead off ops (branches the master no longer has), the pickup-day words of A7-13 (money variant), the B4-14 fee-range line ($150 to $350 visit fee), the $2 and license-lookup ops, the duplicate counter-hold wording. Own steps kept: B8-x01 (the auto-reverse test before DONE), with its safety words.
Licenses: optional and never checked by Rosie (D96); pf.license.check and blocks reworded; the electrical license is the business's own word where the place requires one.
Children: 'Yes: a child may be left' is off at the counter (no child left with the crew); the rating split: 'No: named-only work' is off (every job asks a rating).
Renames: the example's trade words (barbershop, perm, skin fades, hot towel, water heater, sink, pipe, faucet, water line) renamed to door words; 'color' is left as the master's own word (no check flags it as a trade word for this work).
